_doc: MACHINE/LAYOUT MANIFEST (ac-9ahd). Replaces the single `repos_root` key harnesses.json used to carry, which hard-failed the engine on any layout but one specific machine's monorepo checkout. Two keys, deliberately. `targets` says WHERE to look for deploy targets, as path globs resolved against this repo's own directory — so the engine never needs to know whether it sits in a monorepo or a multi-repo split. `harnesses` says which harnesses are enabled on this machine. Nothing more: the engine self-locates its canon from its own path (AC_ROOT), and the org root is AC_ROOT's third parent in every supported layout — e.g. a repos-collection layout at <collection-root>/<org>/software/agent-compounds -> <collection-root>, or a split-repo layout at <home>/<org>/software/agent-compounds -> <home>; both are the identical third-parent rule, just naming a different ancestor as the org root. That derivation was already this script's idiom for the memory-lint path before ac-9ahd generalized it. WHAT this manifest deliberately does NOT carry: per-target policy. Which siblings are actually deploy targets, whether one is `public`, and its `packages` column all stay in infrastructure/ac-deploy-targets.list (path derivable via AC_TARGETS_LIST — see engine/exceptions.sh). Listing target names here too would be a second home for the same fact and the two would drift; `targets` is a search path, the list is the roster, and --all is their intersection.

exceptions._doc: EDITORIAL exclusions only — human judgement, the one hand-maintained input. Technical exclusions (a public target whose harness layer must stay gitignored) are DERIVED by engine/exceptions.sh and never listed here; writing a derived fact down by hand is how the two copies drift. `org_only_skills` names skills that operate the ADOPTER'S OWN organization — a factory, a brain, daily surfaces — and have no job inside an app repo, so they should enter manual-only at org scope rather than deploying full-set. This registry ships none itself (the list is empty by default); an adopter maintaining a private org-level skill set alongside this public one lists those skill names here. Skills named here that enter manual-only at org scope count as zero standing cost to the registry validator's budget. Default policy is unchanged and remains full-set-everywhere: every other asset reaches every managed target. Headroom (20,700 of ~30,000) is what makes that affordable; if it falls below ~2,000 chars, revisit tags-plus-subscriptions.
